einzeiler: Venture capitalist Sarah Guo on investing in frontier AI, robotics, and biology.
kurzfassung: Sarah Guo discusses her approach to early-stage investing at Conviction, focusing on transformative technologies like AI, robotics, and biology. She shares insights on evaluating founders from first principles, navigating the current fast-paced tech environment, and the importance of independent thinking. Additionally, she touches on infrastructure challenges, compute demands, and the value of supporting exceptional talent.
stichpunkte: Co-founding Conviction was driven by a belief in high-agency founders and understanding foundational technologies from first principles.
Evaluating startups involves combining an instinctive read on founders with rigorous research and feedback from trusted peers.
The robotics startup Sunday Robotics exemplifies extreme speed, aiming to deploy general semi-humanoid robots into homes rapidly.
Investing in biology through companies like Chai Discovery challenges conventional biotech wisdom by leveraging AI models to accelerate R&D.
Compute scarcity and regulatory hurdles for energy infrastructure pose significant threats to maintaining technological and national competitiveness.
Open-source models are essential for economic diffusion, allowing businesses to tailor AI applications to diverse, specialized use cases.
Fundraising for a new firm relied on a track record of identifying extraordinary people rather than presenting a rigid, over-engineered narrative.
Early mentorship from established Silicon Valley leaders played a crucial role in shaping a young career in venture capital.

clips.hook: Wanting to hit the brakes while driving 90 miles an hour
clips.text: An investor friend described the current market tension as desperately wanting to slow down yet continuing to accelerate at top speed.

clips.hook: Predicting exponential intelligence for a decade
clips.text: Well-known figures in the field candidly admit to projecting rapid breakthroughs for years without definitive timing.

clips.hook: From basement prototypes to manufactured hardware
clips.text: Rapid iteration allows a robotics team to transition from simple cardboard models in a university basement to fully functional manufactured hardware.

clips.hook: Restricting open source only slows down law-abiding businesses
clips.text: Imposing local barriers on accessible AI models merely hampers domestic commercial users while leaving malicious actors unaffected.

clips.hook: Starting early in venture capital without a traditional pedigree
clips.text: Entering the venture capital industry at a very young age often draws skepticism regarding the actual value provided to experienced founders.

beschreibung:
My guest today is Sarah Guo, founder and managing partner of Conviction, the venture firm she built to back AI-native companies from their earliest days.

Sarah has become one of the most sought-after early-stage investors in AI, often the first check into the companies defining the frontier.

In this conversation, we go inside that frontier: what the small group of people actually building AI believe right now, why some of the field's best researchers are wrestling with their own sense of purpose, and how close we are to robots in the home and a genuine acceleration in scientific discovery.

At the center is Sarah's conviction that no single company will own the future of AI, and what that means for founders, investors, and anyone allocating their time and resources in a world moving this fast.

Our managing editor Dom Cooke wrote a profile of Sarah for Colossus, "Sarah's Wager," on how she built the firm closest to the AI frontier and why she's now betting against its biggest companies.

Please enjoy this conversation with Sarah Guo.
